recipes.name: Potato, Broccoli and Cheese Soup
ingredients_raw: 3 cups fresh broccoli, cooked and drained

steps.text: In a large stock pot saute onion in butter. Add potatoes, water and bouillon cubes. Cover, bring to boil and then reduce heat to medium and cook until potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Remove tough outer skin of broccoli stems and cook broccoli. Once cooked add to soup.
In a blender or food processor puree half of the soup and return to stock pot. Season with salt and pepper.
Add cheese and heat soup through until cheese is melted. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Potato, Broccoli and Cheese Soup
raw_recipe.description: A cheesy, potato broccoli soup that tastes great.

review.reviewBody: I just finished eating this wonderful yummy soup, and it was so easy to make. I did make a few adjustments: I used 4 cups cubed russet potatoes, 1 1lb. bag frozen broccoli flowets, 1 c. chopped onion as I thought 2 cups would be over powering, in place of the bouillion cubes and 5 cups of water I used 2 14oz. cans chicken broth and 1 cup water also added 3 crushed garlic cloves, and only used 8 oz. sharp cheddar cheese. I cooked the broccoli in with the potatoes as other reviewers suggested and then pureed 1/2 the soup and it turned out nice and creamy. This will be a regular in our house during the winter months. Thanks Ruth for sharing this 5 ***** recipe.

This soup was amazing! I did it a little differently though so I guess hard to say for sure this soup recipe was perfect. I melted the margarine/butter and then added 3 stalks of chopped celery, the onion, the broccoli, and potatoes and cooked for about 3 minutes. Then I added about 2 tbsp of flour to coat. Then I added the water and bouillon cubes and I added 2 tsp turmeric and cooked for another 2 minutes and I scooped out the broccoli florets. After about 15 minutes I used a hand blender to blend the soup to a smooth texture and added 1 cup of milk. I let the soup return to a boil and added the cheese and stirred until the cheese was melted. I then added chopped green onion and the broccoli florets on top of the soup. Yum!

I made a couple of changes: I used real butter, unsalted and I used an immersion blender instead of a blender or food processor. I also added a little (1/2 C.) heavy whipping cream. It was delicious, BUT, if you add 1 Knorr Cilantro Mini Cube per 2 1/2 cups of soup, it is OVER THE TOP(5 stars). Obviously, you have to like cilantro, and if you do, you will LOVE this.

I've made my versions of this soup many times. Always delicious and easy to put together. I fully puree the soup in the soup pot using a hand held immersion blender, which works better for me than my food processor. I bought the blender after burning myself trying to transfer hot soup to my food processor. This soup works well when served in small bread bowls. If you can't find rolls that are appropriate for soup, a large bakery roll will do the trick. If your soup is too thin, try adding a tablespoon of corn starch to some cold chicken broth and add it to the hot liquid.

This is such a great recipe. Made a nice sized pot for my family and they loved it! I used 8 cups of water along with 6 cubes of bullion. I also added the broccoli with the potatoes instead of doing it separately. I added 2 tablespoons of flour and 2 cups of milk. Great soup!

I used 6 c of water with 6 veggie cubes(prefer that flavor over chicken), 5 c of cubed potatoes, 2 c onions, 3 c broccoli, garlic and also garlic powder. Followed everything except I put the broccoli to cook with the last 5 mins of the potatoes. Also put the chopped garlic in the last 2 mins of the onions. In the end, added a 1/2 c evaporated milk for some extra creaminess, garlic powder to taste, and used a potato masher to break up everything but still keep some texture. Then added some sliced carrots I had boiling in veggie broth on the side. It was absolutely yummy! Will be making again soon :)

I made it to use leftovers from Thanksgiving. Delicious! I sauteed chopped bacon in some olive oil along with the onions and a diced carrot. When the onions and carrots were soft I added several cloves of garlic chopped and sauteed two more minutes. Then I added 2 cups chicken broth, chopped fresh broccoli and simmered until the broccoli was soft. Then I added leftover mashed potatoes and cheese. I will make it often even if I don't have leftovers.

This is one of the best soup recipes that I have made! I added 3 chopped garlic cloves along with the onions, I also added 2 finely chopped carrots for color. Then I pureed half the soup mixture with out the broccoli, then threw in the raw broccoli and cooked until tender then added the cheese. Delicious!

This is an excellent base for a potato, broccoli, and cheese soup. I've made minor changes just to make it even simpler to prepare with ingredients that I have on hand.

I replaced the water and bouillon cubes with chicken stock. Since the recipe didn't specify, I used red potatoes (and I didn't peel them). I also didn't pre-cook the broccoli, I just chopped it into small pieces that could cook in the stock.

Since I like to have texture in my soup, I didn't blend or process the soup. Instead, I waited until the potatoes and broccoli were cooked all the way through and used a potato masher to just lightly press down on the potatoes and broccoli until the soup was the texture I wanted. I added the cheese at the end and let the soup continue for another 15 minutes or so, just to let it get well incorporated.

I've taken this soup to a potluck at work and people just raved about it and everyone asked for the recipe. It was one that I was pleased to share because it's so easy and so impressive at the same time!

I made this recipe tonight to use up some broccoli and potatoes that were on their way out. I didn't have an onion or butter so I used an onion soup packet. Like other reviewers I added the broccoli to the potatoes after about 10 of the 15 minutes of cooking time. I used an immersion blender to break up enough chunks to get the soup to the creaminess I wanted but still leaving some chunks behind. I only had about a cup of cheese, so that's all I used, and I had a little sour cream that was about to expire (~1/4 cup), so I threw that in too when I added the cheese. 

Great, flexible recipe. The mister added Tabasco to his bowl. I tried it too and it's a delicious way to give it a little kick!
Added 2 shredded carrots and 3 cloves of garlic. Used frozen broccoli and Kinder’s Butter Poultry Seasoning. Stired in 1/4 cup sour cream at the end.

Great recipe. I reduced the serving size, but forgot to reduce the amount of cheese. Extra cheesy soup didn't hurt our feelings. We will do it again soon. Maybe with less cheese. Just to see what the real recipe tastes like.
So easy and quick and absolutely delicious!!!!

I added garlic with the onions, chopped bacon, and added beer later in the process to make up some of my liquid. I think it came to about 1/2 after considering whatever water boiled off during cooking.

Excellent soup for a cold winter Sunday. I did not have cream to add so I thought what is the closest to it.. is Thick Greek Yoghurt, half of that and half of milk. It worked out just fine. Slat and pepper was not enough for my taste buds, so I added a sprinkle of cloves. What a difference in taste. All in all excellent soup and does not take time to do.
Good, but only without the onion. Why anyone would put onion in a creamy, cheesy soup is beyond my comprehension. That’s like putting onion in chocolate ice cream.
This was really good. I thought I was going to need to add a cream base, but after pureeing half the soup, it truly didn’t need it. Added a diced jalapeño for a little kick ;-)
